objective: Report dormant customers so the shop can win them back. `stockroom/report.py` gets `dormant_customers(book: OrderBook, as_of: date, days: int = 90) -> list[tuple[str, date]]`. A `days` below 1 raises `ValueError` (also for an empty book). Only the book's remaining orders matter: cancelled orders and orders placed after `as_of` are ignored entirely, as if they were not in the book. Customers are told apart by the exact `customer` text (no trimming or case folding), and a customer with no remaining order is never reported. A customer is dormant when they have placed no remaining order within `days` days of `as_of`; an order placed on `as_of` itself is always recent. The result has one `(customer, date of their latest remaining order)` pair per dormant customer, oldest date first; customers with the same date come in plain string order of the name (Python `str` comparison, so upper case before lower case). The CLI gets `python -m stockroom dormant --orders FILE --as-of YYYY-MM-DD [--days N]` (`--days` defaults to 90). It prints a count line made with `textutil.plural(count, "dormant customer")` (`1 dormant customer`, `0 dormant customers`, `5 dormant customers`), then one line per dormant customer in the order above: `NAME: last order YYYY-MM-DD, AGE ago`, where AGE is `textutil.plural(n, "day")` for the whole days from that order to `as_of` (`dates.days_between`). A `--days` below 1 is a data error with the message `--days must be at least 1`, and an `--as-of` that is not a date gives the `not a date: ...` message of `dates.parse_date`; data errors exit with code 1, print nothing on stdout and print `stockroom: error: MESSAGE` on stderr. The other commands are unchanged.
acceptance: `dormant_customers` raises `ValueError` when `days` is below 1, also for an empty book

Cancelled orders and orders placed after `as_of` are ignored, customers whose orders are all ignored are not reported, the reported date is the customer's latest remaining order, an order on `as_of` keeps its customer off the list, and an empty book gives `[]`
The list is oldest date first, ties in plain string order of the exact customer text (`Ella` < `Ella ` < `ella`)
`dormant` prints `plural(count, "dormant customer")` and then `NAME: last order DATE, AGE ago` per customer with AGE from `plural(days, "day")`; `--days` defaults to 90
`dormant` with `--days` below 1 or a bad `--as-of` exits with 1, prints nothing on stdout and `stockroom: error: MESSAGE` on stderr
Whether a customer is dormant depends only on the date of their latest remaining order, `as_of` and `days`, as stated (checked over many seeded random books and in the command)

interpretations: An order placed exactly `days` days before `as_of` is within the window: a customer is dormant only when their latest remaining order is more than `days` days old

The window is the `days` days ending on `as_of`: an order placed exactly `days` days before `as_of` is outside it, so a customer is dormant when their latest remaining order is `days` or more days old
